previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for acute on chronic abdominal pain and nausea, consistent with acute on chronic pancreatitis. She had recently left a prior admission AMA but returned due to worsening symptoms and GJ tube dysfunction. Pain and nausea were controlled with IV Dilaudid, Zofran, and Compazine. The GJ tube was successfully replaced by interventional radiology with a preferred type over a wire, and enteral feeds were resumed. Due to poor intake, her Lantus insulin was reduced to 20 units at bedtime, with plans to increase upon improved oral intake. The protonix was switched to Prevacid Solutab for better compatibility with tube administration. The patient declined a final tube function check before discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with a one-week supply of Dilaudid, instructions to follow up with her PCP for medication refills and insulin adjustments, and advised to monitor GJ tube function.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
